- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -1.0) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 1.0) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast peaks or introduce mild downward drag.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; add 0.5–1.0 to forecast if sentiment swings >0.5 in last 5 days.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, and sentiment is neutral or slightly negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.
- When true outcome shows sharp downward trend after a spike, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated +1.0 to +1.5 spikes, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast slope after 3 consecutive positive sentiment days.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of 30-day forecast mean, model is biased low; add 2–5% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model often underestimates true price; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven support.
